newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Mackie revises 1996 results, set rights issue.
newsitem.headline: Mackie revises 1996 results, set rights issue.

text.p: Mackie International Group Plc said on Tuesday that it was restating its 1996 preliminary results following a full financial and management review.

Its revised audited financial statements show a turnover of 12.6 million sterling in 1996 against 17.7 million previously and a loss before tax of 7.2 million compared with a previously announced loss of 0.4 million.
The group also announced a five-for-two rights issue to raise a net 5.25 million sterling for completion of its foundry, restructuring costs and working capital.
Mackie said a restructuring programme had been put in place for its textile operations together with a substantial reduction in central overhead costs.

"The position that Mackie is in has required firm and direct management action. The restatement of results, operational restructuring and rights issue put a line under the company's recent problems and provide the basis for returning the businesses to profitability in the medium term," chief executive Sul Sahota said.
Sahota, who was appointed in March, said the company would now apply to the London and Irish Stock Exchanges to have the temporary suspension of its shares lifted.
The shares were suspended after certain matters came to the attention of the board which it considered might lead to a material restatement of the group's financial results.
Sahota said the suspension should be lifted on July 3, the day after an extraordinary meeting to approve the rights issue.
